mesencephalic progenitor cells, isolated from the germinal regions of the fetal rat brain, are mitotically active, express the progenitor cell markers, can be readily infected by a retrovirus, and can be differentiated into dopaminergic neurons by a combination of cytokines.
mesencephalic progenitor cells can be induced to become dopamine neurons by the addition of interleukin-1 and glial-derived neurotrophic factors.
mesencephalic progenitor cells can be expanded for a long period of time and can be induced to express a DA neuron phenotype by the cytokine IL-1.

understanding the mechanisms that control the development of neurons in the central nervous system.
